identificationModule.officialTitle: Efficacy of Antiplatelet Therapy for the Treatment of Chronic Recalcitrant Urticaria

descriptionModule.briefSummary: This study compares the combination of antiplatelets and antihistamine versus antihistamine alone for the treatment of chronic spontaneous urticaria
descriptionModule.detailedDescription: This study is a randomized control trial comparing the effectiveness of the combination of antiplatelets and antihistamine and antihistamine alone for the treatment of chronic spontaneous urticaria

designInfo.interventionModelDescription: Patients diagnosed with chronic urticaria will be assigned to 2 treatment arms. 1. high dose antihistamine with antiplatelets; and 2. high dose antihistamine alone.

armGroups.label: Desloratadine plus cilostazol and dipyridamole
armGroups.description: Oral desloratadine 20 mg/day (antihistamine) in conjunction with cilostazol 150 mg/day and dipyridamole 50 mg/day (antiplatelets) for 4 weeks
interventionNames: Drug: Desloratadine plus cilostazol and dipyridamole

interventions.name: Desloratadine plus cilostazol and dipyridamole
interventions.description: Desloratadine 20 mg/day plus cilostazol 150 mg/day and dipyridamole 50 mg/day

primaryOutcomes.description: Urticaria activity score over 7 days (UAS7): scores 0-42 from mild to severe

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Chronic spontaneous urticaria

D-dimer levels over 500 ng/ml

Not respond to a conventional dose of antihistamine

Exclusion Criteria:

Are taking aspirin

Have bleeding tendency

Have concurrent severe medical illnesses
